question: GQ-004
subject: replacing the sampled estimate with a census
why: The 105 rested on 20-40 titles per subject. Computing the 95% interval gave 42-186 — a range so wide the point estimate was more precise-looking than the evidence supported. The science-fiction band alone spanned 0-39 from a single hit in 40 titles.
what_changed: Five of the six pools are small enough to check in full. A census has no sampling error, and it cost one query each.

census.subject: Science fiction
census.note: still sampled — pool too large for a single query

reading: 124 new books COUNTED across five subjects, plus a sampled estimate of ~13 for science fiction. The sampled figures understated every weak subject: Essays 26 -> 37, Cookery 21 -> 30, Detective 4 -> 14. Small samples on small pools were noisy in the pessimistic direction.
honest_note: Science fiction remains sampled at 40 of 535. It is also the lowest-yield subject measured, so its contribution is small either way — but the total is "124 counted + ~13 estimated", not a single clean number.
